interpretive.rule: Willful under §1681n = objectively unreasonable interpretation of statute (reckless disregard); opens institutional-policy willfulness theory + punitive damages
Bare procedural FCRA violation without concrete harm ≠ Article III standing; must show real harm or realistic risk of harm from inaccuracy
Concrete injury requires downstream disclosure to third party; inaccuracy in file never disclosed = no standing; defamation-by-publication analogy

chexsystems_action_plan.step_1: Request full ChexSystems file + complete disclosure log under §1681g. Identify every subscriber pull and date.
chexsystems_action_plan.step_2: Identify each inaccurate entry. Document which bank denial corresponds to which entry (standing anchor per TransUnion).
chexsystems_action_plan.step_3: If any entry resulted from identity theft (SSN theft, fraudulent account): file FTC identity theft report at IdentityTheft.gov FIRST.
chexsystems_action_plan.step_4: Submit §1681c-2 blocking request to ChexSystems with FTC report + proof of identity + identification of entries to block. ChexSystems must block within 4 business days.
chexsystems_action_plan.step_5: If ChexSystems fails to block within 4 days OR wrongfully rescinds the block: §1681n willful violation (Safeco recklessness standard). Statutory $100-$1,000 per violation + punitive.

treasury_downstream_plan.note: If Treasury identity theft resulted in any CRA reporting (Equifax, Experian, TransUnion, ChexSystems, LexisNexis), apply same §1681c-2 blocking procedure. The FTC identity theft report covers all downstream CRA reporting from a single theft event.

standing_documentation_checklist: Date of each ChexSystems or CRA inquiry (subscriber pulls from disclosure log)
Identity of subscriber (bank name or creditor name)
Adverse action taken (account denial letter, credit denial, employment denial)
Dollar amount of harm if quantifiable (account fees avoided, higher interest rate, etc.)
Emotional distress harm if documented (medical records, contemporaneous notes)

sol.rule: 2 years from date plaintiff discovered violation, or 5 years from date violation occurred, whichever is earlier. §1681p.
sol.ongoing_reporting_note: Each new disclosure of an inaccurate report to a third party is a new violation with a new SOL clock. A ChexSystems entry that was disclosed to a bank in 2024 AND in 2026 produces two separate violations, each with its own 2-year discovery clock.
